summary: The dedup-by-name-on-first-yield approach stops duplicate reporting but yields the intermediate, pre-substitution hashed_name for adjustable files (exactly the base.css case in the bug report), since every adjustable path is already marked processed during the initial single pass and the multi-pass loop's later, corrected hashed_name is then silently dropped. This produces incorrect '<file> as <hash>' output and would feed subclasses (WhiteNoise, S3 backends) the wrong intermediate file instead of the final one, which is the exact regression the original issue warned about.

issues.description: processed_files accumulates every path (including adjustable ones) during the first single pass, so the second loop's substitution passes never yield for those files again — even when later passes change the final hashed_name. Callers (and post_process consumers/subclasses) get the stale first-pass hash rather than the true final hash stored in hashed_files/the manifest.

Dedup-by-first-occurrence is the wrong invariant for this problem; correctness requires reporting the LAST (final, stabilized) hashed_name per adjustable file, not the first. A dict keyed by name updated each pass and yielded once after the loop settles would give correct behavior; the set-based first-seen approach is a structurally incorrect fix, not merely a style issue.
